description.value: The Langley Learning Farm is a community-based food production demonstration site located at the Derek Doubleday Arboretum on parkland within the Agricultural Land Reserve. Established in September 2020, it is a student-led initiative where Grade 11/12 students from Langley Secondary School tend growing beds, a hoop house, and a fruit-bearing hedgerow as part of an experiential Environmental Science course. Public informational signage explains the project, making it a modest stop for cyclists curious about urban agriculture and food security efforts in the Fraser Valley.

raw_osm.description: The Langley Learning Farm teaches community-based food production. A partnership of the Langley Sustainable Agriculture Foundation, Langley Environmental Partners Society, and Langley Secondary School supports student-led farming and food security.
raw_osm.name: The Learning Farm

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms this is an educational farm at the Derek Doubleday Arboretum, operated as a student-led project for Grade 11/12 students from Langley Secondary School in partnership with LSAF and LEPS. No cyclist amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water refill) are mentioned anywhere on the website or in OSM tags. The contact page lists an LSAF organizational address (19915-37A Avenue) which appears to be the foundation's office, not the farm site itself.
concerns: Address listed (19915-37A Avenue, Langley, BC V3A 2S8) is the LSAF organizational office from the contact page, not the farm's physical location at Derek Doubleday Arboretum — OSM coordinates should be treated as more reliable for the farm site.
No phone number available in OSM or on website.
Public access hours and drop-in visitor policy are not described anywhere on the website; the farm appears primarily oriented toward scheduled student groups.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is primarily a school-program educational facility with no confirmed public drop-in access and no cyclist amenities documented. It is situated within a public arboretum which may offer incidental interest to touring cyclists, but insufficient evidence exists to confirm it functions as a publicly accessible attraction suitable for a WWC listing.
enrichment_extras.notes: The farm is tagged in OSM as garden:type=show_garden, suggesting some public-facing intent, but the website text focuses entirely on student programming. Verification of public access policy would be needed before including in the directory.
